topic: Codex Command Center: A Local Desktop Control Center for Codex Projects

key_points: PRIMARY SUBJECT. Self-description: 'A local desktop control center for organizing Codex projects, engineering tasks, sessions, Git changes, Skills, and MCP configuration' - a Windows-first, local-first Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript desktop workspace.

Explicit positioning as an ORGANIZING LAYER, not an executor: 'Codex does the reasoning, editing, commands, and tests. Codex Command Center keeps the surrounding engineering workflow understandable and resumable.' README states it is intentionally smaller than an IDE, terminal emulator, chat client, or advanced Git GUI.

Core loop is a 5-stage pipeline: Project -> Task -> Codex Session -> File Changes -> Result. Typical flow: add a repository, create/select an engineering task, launch or resume Codex, review indexed sessions, inspect Git changes, then continue/complete/block the task.

Features: project registration (branch, Git state, task counts, recent activity); lightweight task tracking with Planned/Active/Completed/Blocked states; local Codex session metadata indexing WITHOUT mutating Codex session files; session-to-task linking; Codex CLI launch + resume; Git review (branch, staged/unstaged, working-tree state, per-file diffs, stage/unstage/commit); Codex environment visibility (CLI path/version, redacted config previews, Skills discovery, MCP server summaries).

Local-first guarantees are unusually explicit: state is local JSON under the user's local app data dir; registered projects are path references only (source code is NOT copied into app storage); NO telemetry, analytics, accounts, cloud sync, source-code upload, session upload, or Git-diff upload. Config previews redact lines that look like keys/tokens/secrets/passwords.

Architecture: React+TypeScript frontend (src/), Tauri 2 desktop shell (src-tauri/), Rust native commands for filesystem/process-launch/Git/Codex-indexing/Skills/MCP, and local Codex CLI + Git CLI calls. AGENTS.md forbids background services and long-running supervisors, and mandates small explicit native commands.

Scope discipline is codified in AGENTS.md: keep it Codex-only; explicitly do NOT add Claude/Gemini support, provider switching, OAuth provider management, remote SSH orchestration, cloud sync, telemetry, accounts, or marketplace features. Non-goals in ROADMAP.md repeat this and add 'no fabricated usage metrics, testimonials, or community activity'.

Honest lineage: evolved from the open-source CodMate project by Loocor; Apache-2.0 attribution preserved in LICENSE, NOTICE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. README explicitly says it 'should not be described as built entirely from scratch'. Historical commit 'feat: transform CodMate into Codex Command Center' (2026-08-17) confirms the fork point. Disclaimer states it is not an official OpenAI product.

VERIFIED REPO FACTS (GitHub API, 2026-10-01): Apache-2.0; 201 stars / 1 fork / 5 contributors; created 2026-08-17; 420 commits total; TypeScript 49.5 KB, Rust 37.5 KB, CSS 8.8 KB; 2 releases - v0.1.0 (2026-08-20) and v0.1.1 (2026-08-29), 3 assets each (NSIS setup .exe, MSI, standalone .exe) plus SHA256SUMS.txt, 14 cumulative downloads.

MAINTENANCE SIGNAL (verified): the last non-dependabot, non-docs code commit is 'fix: harden local state persistence' on 2026-08-29. Every commit since (through 2026-10-01) is Dependabot bumps or changelog docs. Of 8 non-dependency issues, all are closed with zero comments; the only 2 open issues (as of 2026-10-01) are Dependabot PRs (#26 npm, #27 cargo). Discussions: 1 thread. Star trend on third-party trackers is flat-to-down (-4 stars over 10 days, vibecrowd.ai).

Known limitations stated in the v0.1.0 changelog: Windows-first (other desktop platforms are not documented release targets); installers are UNSIGNED unless the maintainer adds code signing; the app expects local Codex CLI and Git to be on PATH. Requirements: Windows 11 primary, Node.js 24, Rust/Cargo for native builds, Git and Codex CLI on PATH.

The category leader by adoption (verified 2026-10-01: 3,384 stars / 363 forks / AGPL-3.0 / TypeScript / 145 open issues / last push 2026-10-01). Positioned as an 'Agent Orchestration Command Center' supporting Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.

Depth of orchestration C3 does not attempt: Git worktree sub-agents for true parallel development on isolated branches, Auto Run & Playbooks (file-system task runner batch-processing markdown checklists through AI sessions), and Group Chat with a moderator AI routing between agents.

Operational features that overlap C3's territory but go further: mobile remote control via built-in web server + QR code + Cloudflare tunneling, a full maestro-cli for headless/cron/CI operation, message queueing while an agent is busy, and agent resilience that auto-resends a prompt killed by 529 Overloaded or a spent quota.

Session Discovery is the direct analogue of C3's indexing: it imports existing sessions from all supported providers, including conversations from before Maestro was installed - but Maestro also owns the live session surface (AI Terminal + Command Terminal dual mode), while C3 indexes metadata and hands execution to the Codex CLI.

Also ships Cost Tracking per session/global, a Usage Dashboard with heatmaps and CSV export, Document Graph, File Explorer with syntax highlighting, and first-class previews for JSON/JSONL/CSV/Parquet/audio/video.

CONTRAST: multi-engine by design and much heavier; C3's bet is Codex-only focus plus a local ledger, Maestro's is breadth of engines plus live orchestration. AGPL-3.0 vs C3's Apache-2.0 is also a material license difference for commercial embedding.

Team-oriented 'command center for all things agentic' from Preset (the Superset company). Verified 2026-10-01: 1,419 stars / 130 forks / TypeScript / 247 open issues / last push 2026-10-01 / homepage agor.live.

Differentiator is MULTIPLAYER collaboration: real-time shared canvas and multi-user sessions on top of git-worktree isolation - built for a team sharing agent work, not one developer's local ledger. Topics include multiplayer, real-time-collaboration, and canvas.

Supports Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI across a shared board; MCP-aware. Its worktree + canvas model competes with C3's 'task -> session' linking but targets a collaborative surface rather than a Windows desktop app.
CONTRAST: web/team-first and open-source with a hosted dimension, vs C3's single-user, no-account, Windows-local desktop posture.

The most-starred macOS-specific agent surface (verified 2026-10-01: 1,124 stars / 127 forks / Swift / Apache-2.0 / homepage erha19.github.io/ping-island). A Dynamic Island-style notch UI for managing all AI coding agents.

Complements rather than competes: it is an ATTENTION layer (compact until a session needs approval or input; approve/deny tools from the notch; one-click return to iTerm2/Ghostty/Terminal.app/tmux/IDE window) rather than a project/task ledger.

Extremely broad client coverage (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Qwen Code, Kimi, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, OpenClaw, and more), including SSH terminal support that bootstraps a remote PingIslandBridge and forwards remote Codex app-server activity into the local Island UI.

Relevant to C3's thesis because its 'Codex hook + app-server sync' and rollout-parsing fallback show that reading Codex's local session/rollout data is a well-established integration path - the same substrate C3 indexes for its session discovery.
CONTRAST: macOS/Swift and notification-first; C3 is Windows/TypeScript+Rust and organizing-first. A Windows user gets no Ping Island equivalent from it today.

Direct competitor in the multi-agent dashboard space for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. Verified 2026-10-01: 392 stars / 22 forks / Apache-2.0 / TypeScript / 0 open issues / last push 2026-09-16 (less fresh than C3's 2026-10-01 push).

Its README's origin story is the clearest articulation of the pain C3 also targets: 'Visual chaos - my desktop was covered in Claude Code terminals. I constantly lost track of which window was running which task' plus edit conflicts and opaque token bills.

Solves it with automatic Git worktree isolation per task, per-task provider selection to route cheap models to simple tasks (cost savings), phone-based progress monitoring, MCP integration, and a PTY + output parser + JSON-Patch MsgStore architecture.
Adds a 'Team Mode' for real multi-agent collaboration and mobile access - both beyond C3's scope.

CONTRAST: owns the live execution surface (PTY-driven agents) and optimizes on cost/model routing; C3 deliberately refuses provider switching and terminal emulation, and instead makes the pre-existing Codex CLI session history navigable.

Closest in spirit to C3's 'command center' framing but multi-engine and far deeper operationally (verified 2026-10-01: 175 stars / 20 forks / Python / local-first topic / last push 2026-10-01, actively developed).

Core surfaces: one board across eight engines, a flow canvas and project tree, split conversations, cross-session search, durable queues with one inbox, worker specialization, and 'sessions that coordinate without you'.

Stands out for agent-ops maturity: answer Claude Code permission prompts inline from the dashboard, plan-to-fleet import into a WatchTower queue, fresh worktree spawns on feat/<slug> branches, headless spawn with follow-up, resume-on-demand via auto-spawned headless sessions.

Also tracks usage/cost per engine against plan limits with cache-adjusted rankings, a model deny-list policy, and auto-fix deploys that poll Vercel and spawn a /fix-deploy session on production errors.

CONTRAST: it is a control plane that supervises and intervenes in live agents; C3 is a read-mostly organizer of Codex work and explicitly declines to be a chat client or terminal. CCC is also Python + browser-served, not a signed Windows Tauri binary.

The official incumbent and the elephant in the room: OpenAI's own Codex desktop app, announced for macOS on 2026-02-02 and extended to Windows on 2026-03-04 (distributed via the Microsoft Store). OpenAI itself calls it a 'command center for agents' - the exact phrase C3 borrows.

Official app primitives: parallel agents with isolated Git worktrees, reusable Skills, and Automations for scheduled/triggered recurring work (triage, CI-failure summaries, security scans) routed into a human review queue.

Windows build adds a Windows-native OS-level sandbox (restricted tokens, filesystem ACLs, dedicated sandbox users, explicit escalation approval), PowerShell-first execution, and optional WSL project support. Available across all ChatGPT tiers alongside CLI, IDE extension, and cloud under one account.

CRITICAL STRATEGIC POINT for the review: the official app is account-bound and cloud-tied (model inference in the cloud, work tied to a ChatGPT account), and it supervises live agent work. It does NOT organize your pre-existing local Codex session history, local Skills folders, MCP config, or per-repo task ledger - which is precisely the gap C3 targets.

Also note the naming collision: C3 shares the 'command center' framing with a first-party product on the same platform (Windows), so its value must be argued as complementary metadata/ledger layer rather than as an orchestrator.

stats.fact: Codex weekly active users grew from under 1 million in February 2026 to more than 8 million by roughly July 20, 2026 (~7-8x in five months): <1M (Feb 2026), ~2M (Mar 5), ~3M (Apr 8), 4M+ (Apr 21), 5M+ (Jun 2), 6M (Jul 12), 7M (Jul 13), 8M+ (~Jul 20).
Combined weekly actives across Codex and the newly launched ChatGPT Work agent reached roughly 10 million by 2026-07-21, per OpenAI.
The @openai/codex npm package was downloaded 888,417,733 times in the 30 days from 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-29 - a scale indicator for how many Codex CLI installs exist to organize.
Codex CLI, the open-source terminal agent, passed 99,624 GitHub stars by 2026-07-19 and grew npm downloads from 82,000 (April 2025) to 41.8 million (May 2026).

OpenAI's official Codex desktop app timeline: announced for macOS 2026-02-02, extended to Windows 2026-03-04 via the Microsoft Store, with the Windows sandbox engineering explainer published 2026-05-13.

Codex Command Center releases: v0.1.0 on 2026-08-20 and v0.1.1 on 2026-08-29, each shipping a NSIS setup .exe, an MSI, a standalone .exe and SHA256SUMS.txt - 14 cumulative downloads across both releases.

Between 2026-08-29 and 2026-10-01 every commit was a Dependabot bump or changelog doc edit; the only 2 open issues are Dependabot PRs (#26 npm, #27 cargo) and all 8 non-dependency issues are closed with zero comments.

Third-party star tracking shows flat-to-declining interest: 203 stars with -4 stars measured over a 10-day window (~2026-09-11 to 2026-09-21), against 1 fork and 0 open issues at the time of that snapshot.

The project's Windows binaries are currently unsigned, and Windows 11 is the primary supported platform; Node.js 24, Rust/Cargo, Git on PATH and Codex CLI on PATH are required for source builds and for the app's Git/Codex actions to function.

angles: The 'organizing layer' thesis: as Codex weekly users went from <1M to 8M+, the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to remembering what you were doing - which repo, which task, which session, which uncommitted diff. C3's Project -> Task -> Session -> Changes -> Result loop is an answer to context sprawl, not to code generation.

Complementarity with the official Codex app, not competition: OpenAI's app supervises live agents and orchestrates new work (worktrees, Skills, Automations) but is account/cloud-bound and does not curate your existing local Codex history, local Skills folders, or MCP config per repo. C3 is the ledger over that history. Frame it as 'the filing cabinet next to the workbench'.

Windows-first as a deliberate wedge: OpenAI only reached Windows on 2026-03-04, and most of the agent-dashboard ecosystem is macOS-centric (Ping Island is Swift/macOS) or browser-served (CCC is Python + browser). A native Windows 11 Tauri app that speaks PowerShell-era Windows dev workflow is a defensible niche - and also its biggest constraint.

Local-first as a trust posture, not a feature list: path references instead of copied source code, redacted config previews, no telemetry/accounts/cloud sync, and non-mutating reads of Codex session files. This is the strongest argument for developers who will not upload a client codebase - and it is verifiable in the README/AGENTS.md, not just marketing.

Deliberate smallness as a design position worth reviewing fairly: AGENTS.md forbids IDE/editor/terminal-emulator/chat-client/advanced-Git behavior and forbids background supervisors. Reviewers should ask whether 'smaller than an IDE' is discipline or a ceiling - the ROADMAP's near-term items (search, completion summaries, session parsing resilience, accessibility) suggest the maintainer knows the ceiling is the risk.

The Codex-only bet cuts both ways: refusing Claude/Gemini/provider-switching and marketplace features keeps the product coherent and trustworthy (no half-supported engines), but every multi-engine competitor (Maestro, Agor, CCC, Agent Tower) can absorb a Codex-only user's next need. A reader's decision hinges on whether they are single-engine by conviction.

REVIEWER'S HONEST CAVEAT - momentum and maintenance risk: 201 stars is real but small (ranked well below the 1,000+ leaders), 14 release downloads undercuts the star count, the last substantive code commit predates 2026-09-01, and the only open issues are Dependabot PRs. The review must state plainly that this is an early, single-maintainer, unsigned-installer v0.1.x project whose roadmap is explicitly 'not a dated commitment' - useful now, but evaluate on the code and the local-first guarantees, not on momentum.

Inherited-code transparency as a trust signal: the README names CodMate/Loocor, keeps Apache-2.0 NOTICE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, and says outright it 'should not be described as built entirely from scratch' - a refreshing contrast to the many 'from scratch' claims in this crowded niche.

Safety-by-redaction: configuration previews strip lines resembling keys/tokens/secrets, and error messages are specified to be human-readable ('Codex CLI was not found.'), with raw secrets/tokens/stack traces banned from normal UI. Worth calling out because agent tooling routinely leaks exactly these.

Adoption path friction as a real deciding factor: unsigned Windows installers plus Node 24/Rust/Cargo/Git/Codex-CLI-on-PATH requirements mean the easy path is downloading a .exe and accepting the unsigned-binary warning. Readers need a clear 'easiest install vs source build' decision tree.
